newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel CPI-linked bonds continue higher.
newsitem.headline: Israel CPI-linked bonds continue higher.

text.p: Israeli CPI-linked bonds closed higher on Wednesday on expectations of a tight supply of these bonds and a high July consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.17 pct to 111.49
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.25 pct to 111.87
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.11 pct to 110.11
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.08 pct to 111.44
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.02 pct to 108.51
Volume including Makams was an average 188 million shekels.

"The market continued the trend of the last few days. Demand for CPI-linked bonds was up, especially long bonds, and prices rose significantly," said Zvi Stepak, managing director of Meitav Investments and Securities.
"Yields to maturity of some of the long bonds are down to 3.75-3.78," he said.
Stepak said the falling yields were due to a tight supply of CPI-linked bonds.

Government bond redemptions are expected to total about four billion shekels in August against issues of 1.6 billion shekels; a successful privatisation process and higher tax revenues are all expected to lessen the government's need to raise debt on the bond market.
Traders said that the shortage was expected to affect all government bonds, but especially CPI-linked bonds.

The Treasury said on Wednesday it would issue 1.6 billion shekels worth of bonds in August. Of these issues, 900 million shekels would be in CPI-linked bonds and 700 million shekels in unlinked bonds. The Treasury said it would not issue any dollar-linked bonds in August.

"The unlinked share of new bond issues against total issues is growing. The government wants to gradually phase out CPI-linked bonds because linked instruments are more damaging to the economy," Stepak said.
"The market estimates that July's CPI will be a high 0.9 to 1.1 percent, mainly because of high housing prices" said Ronen Elgali of United Mizrahi Bank.
He said the expected high CPI was causing traders to take cover in CPI-linked instruments and to shun unlinked bonds and depress their prices.
"Today prices of fixed-interest unlinked bonds had most of the falls because of fears that interest rates may go up on a high July CPI," Stepak said.
The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices in July and August.
July's CPI will be published on August 15.
Prices of dollar-linked bonds closed slightly higher on the rise of the dollar against the shekel on Tuesday, traders said.
The shekel's representative rate was fixed stable against the dollar on Wednesday. The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5410 shekels compared with 3.5440 on Tuesday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.54 shekels)
